Brazilian officials first raised concerns with Apple nearly three months ago about gambling apps being accessible to minors, and Apple has now been given five business days to provide further details on the safeguards in place on its App Store. Read on for the full details.

Apple faces pressure over regulation and age verification

Last April, Brazilian officials notified both Apple and Google separately about a suspected lack of age restrictions on gambling apps in their app stores.

At the time, the National Secretariat for Digital Rights (Sedigi) and the National Consumer Secretariat (Senacon) each wrote to the two companies, asking whether a “large number” of apps offered or helped minors access gambling platforms.

Brazil recently passed a new law called the Digital Rights of Children and Adolescents Act (ECA Digital), which requires app stores to restrict minors' exposure to gambling content. Apple subsequently introduced age verification measures for apps rated 18 and above in the country.

However, officials said their preliminary investigation found that several gambling apps appeared to lack proper age restrictions or federal authorisation, casting doubt on how these safeguards were being enforced.

Although the full content of Apple's response has not been made public, the relevant departments now say that Apple has answered most of the questions in the first round. Nonetheless, the authorities are still asking for more information.

The following was published by Brazil's Ministry of Justice and Public Security via Canaltech:

The clarifications requested include: how regulatory authorisation is verified for apps listed in Brazil; the technical criteria used to distinguish simulation apps from those involving real-money gambling, including cases where functionality is hidden or altered after approval; and the mechanisms in place to prevent minors from accessing inappropriate content. Also requested is information on proactive monitoring procedures, risk-ranking criteria, the average takedown time after detection, and the published timeline for implementing remedial measures, including

The two departments said Google's response was less satisfactory and demanded more detailed explanations, including how it verifies authorised operators, how it monitors apps whose licences have been suspended or expired, how it measures enforcement effectiveness, and how it prevents minors from finding or downloading gambling apps.

The two departments ultimately requested that Apple and Google publish their responses, while allowing confidential material to be submitted separately under restricted access.
